title: Heads Visible Down the Line
statement:
People stand in a line, all facing right. heights[i] is the height of person i, and all heights are different.

Person i can see person j (with j > i) if everybody standing strictly between them is shorter than both of them. Return an array where entry i is the number of people that person i can see.

examples.why: Person 0 (height 5) sees 2, 3, 4 and 6, but not the 1, which hides behind the 3. Person 2 (height 3) sees the 1 and the 4; the 4 then blocks the 6.
Each person sees only the next one: that taller person blocks everyone behind.
Seeing someone is not the same as being taller than everyone after. Person 0 sees the 3, and the 3 hides the shorter people behind it.

hints: Person i sees the next person always. After that, they keep seeing people only while each new person is taller than everyone seen so far. When do they stop?

Scan from the right. Person i will see every person to their right that is shorter than i and not hidden, plus the first one who is taller. Shorter people that i sees are hidden from everyone further left, behind i.

Keep a stack of heights from the right, decreasing from bottom to top. For person i, pop every height smaller than heights[i], counting each pop; if the stack is still non-empty, add one more for the taller person on top. Then push heights[i].

explain.intuition:
Walk the line from the right end towards the left, and keep a stack of the people who are still visible to someone coming from the left. When person i arrives, every person on the stack shorter than i is someone i can see: nobody between them is taller, or they would have hidden that person and removed them from the stack already. Pop them all and count them.

After the pops, if the stack is not empty, its top is the first person taller than i, and i sees that person too, but nobody behind them. The popped people are now hidden behind i for everyone to the left, so it is safe to drop them for good. Then push i. Each person is pushed and popped once, so the whole scan is O(n). It is the "next greater element" stack, with a count on the side.
steps: Create ans of zeros and an empty stack.
While the stack is non-empty and its top is less than heights[i], pop it and add 1 to ans[i].
If the stack is still non-empty, add 1 more: the taller person on top.
pitfalls: Counting only the people shorter than i. The first taller person is seen too, as in [4, 3, 2, 1], where person 0 sees the 3.
Counting everyone shorter than i to the right. In [5, 2, 3, 1, 4, 6] the 1 is shorter than the 5 but hidden behind the 3.
Scanning from the left with the same stack. It answers 'who sees me', not 'whom do I see'.

solutions.title: Look right from every person
solutions.idea: For each i, walk right while tracking the tallest person passed. Person j is visible when they are taller than everyone in between; stop after the first person taller than i.

solutions.title: Monotonic stack from the right
solutions.idea: The stack holds the people still visible from the left, decreasing towards the top. Person i pops and sees the shorter ones, then sees the taller one left on top.

followups: Heights may now repeat, and an equal height blocks the view. What changes in the pop condition and the extra +1?
Return, for each person, the farthest person they can see instead of the count.
